Watchability round 1 from the owner of PaperTrades.AI (Fri Oct 30, 11:40 p.m. ET; Season 1, day 4 of 32). NOT a trading turn; nothing in your books changes. The owner: "keep polishing the watchability on everything: website, ledger, transactions, social media. It could turn into a real thing people follow. Ask all models for further assistance." The owner's rule: majority wins (2 of 3 AIs). Answer honestly and disagree where you disagree.

Claude audited the live site on a 390px phone and a desktop tonight. Facts: the site is one static page on GitHub Pages (no accounts, no cookies, no server); every check-in rebuilds it; posts go to Telegram (every move), X (just started: daily race card and lead changes), Instagram (daily carousel, stories; currently paused by Meta's request limit) and a read-only Discord. Posts never show added-up totals before Nov 28. Receipt cards ("the bet behind it") and X link replies are being decided in a separate round, so they are not repeated here.

WEBSITE: FIRST IMPRESSION
W1. First-visit hero. Today the "Which AI makes the most money in real markets?" explainer sits on the THIRD phone screen, under standings and moments. A first-time visitor (no saved visit in their browser) sees one compact card at the very top: "Claude vs Gemini vs ChatGPT · C$100,000 of pretend money each · 10 races · real prices · Oct 28 to Nov 28", who leads overall, and two buttons: "See the races" and "Follow live". Returning visitors don't see it (it can be reopened from About). [Claude: AGREE]
W2. "Since your last visit" strip for returning visitors: the browser remembers when they last looked (stored only in their browser), and the top shows e.g. "Since you were here 6 h ago: 2 lead changes · Gemini won 2 bets · Claude sold Bitcoin", built from the existing Moments list, each line tappable. Hidden if nothing happened or the last visit was under 15 minutes ago. [Claude: AGREE]

WEBSITE: NUMBERS THAT ARE RIGHT BUT READ WRONG (owner's standing rule)
W3. (a) "Last trade: Sell Bitcoin USD (C$39,604): −C$396 profit" becomes "... loss C$396". (b) "−0.0%" (shown in red) and "−C$0" become "0.0%" / "C$0". (c) A "MARKET RISK: HIGH" badge on a race where that AI is 100% cash becomes "All cash · no market risk now" (the race's risk level stays in the tooltip). (d) The crown line "👑 Gemini leads overall +C$15,925 · 2nd ChatGPT −C$2,852 · leads 4 of 10 races" reads as if ChatGPT leads 4 races; reorder to "👑 Gemini leads overall +C$15,925 · leads 4 of 10 races · 2nd ChatGPT −C$2,852". (e) All in sports "2nd Claude +C$0" when Claude hasn't bet yet becomes "Claude: no bets yet". (f) A benchmark shown as a bare dash ("Vs. the S&P 500: —") says "not available yet". [Claude: AGREE]
W4. The AI vs AI tab says "profits are not added together during the month", but the header now shows each AI's overall total. Reword to: "Each race is scored on its own. The overall figure at the top adds the ten up (China converted to C$), the same way the winner is decided on Nov 28." And label the two different leads clearly everywhere: "👑 Leads overall (total profit: this decides the winner)" vs "Most races led: Claude, 5 of 10". Today Gemini wears the crown in the header while the AI vs AI tab crowns Claude "LEADS THE MOST RACES", so a newcomer can't tell who is winning. [Claude: AGREE]

WEBSITE: PHONES
W5. Ledger tables become stacked cards on phones (under 600px): each row of the Decision log, Holdings and Every trade tables shows as a card: time · race · action on one line, then the full text at full width. Today on a 390px phone the time column wraps into about 12 lines and the text is cut off at the right edge (e.g. "Won NCAAF: Tu... moneyline (Tu @ Charlotte 4"). [Claude: AGREE]
W6. Shorter times. Lists show one time, "Oct 30, 11:14 p.m. ET"; tapping or hovering it shows UTC and Hong Kong time. Today almost every line carries three time zones ("Oct 30, 11:14 p.m. ET (Oct 31, 03:14 UTC · Oct 31, 11:14 a.m. HKT)"), 2 to 3 lines per item on a phone. China-race items keep Beijing time next to ET. "Last updated" is said once per page ("Values as of 11:14 p.m. ET · 13 min ago") instead of on each of the ten race cards. [Claude: AGREE]
W7. Home first screen: the UTC clock becomes the race's own clock in ET (the countdown stays), and service-status pills such as "Instagram posts delayed" move off the first screen into the status box in Rules & Audit (the LIVE box links there). [Claude: AGREE]

WEBSITE: CHARTS AND SCOREBOARD
W8. Chart date labels: when a chart covers a few days the axis repeats dates ("Oct 29, Oct 29, Oct 30, Oct 30"); label once per day, or with times ("Oct 29, 6 a.m.") when it covers under 3 days. [Claude: AGREE]
W9. Scoreboard: rank the ten main races on their own; the two All in side races get their own small row underneath labelled "Side race". Today All in: trading is ranked "1st" and All in: sports "3rd" inside the main list. [Claude: AGREE]
W10. Best Risk Manager: show "higher is better" next to the risk scores and explain negatives in one line ("negative = lost money; closer to zero is better"). No change to the formula all three agreed. [Claude: AGREE]

SOCIAL AND TRANSACTIONS
W11. "Tonight's slate" (sports): each evening at 6:30 p.m. ET, one card on Telegram, X and an Instagram story listing every open bet of all three AIs on that night's games, side by side: game, start time (ET), each AI's pick, odds and stake. Skipped when there are no open bets. Builds anticipation; the result cards (now with final scores) close the loop. [Claude: AGREE]
W12. "Day N preview" at 9:05 a.m. ET on weekdays: one card with today's scheduled events (data releases, earnings, games) and each AI's own plan for the day in one line, taken from its published 24-hour plan. Same channels. Gives followers a morning appointment. [Claude: AGREE]
W13. The robot mascots on every share card and post picture: a small robot head next to the AI's name (the same robots the site now uses, with their shape cues), so a viewer recognises the AI before reading. Colours unchanged. [Claude: AGREE]
W14. Lead-change posts add rivalry context from numbers we already have: how long the previous lead lasted and how many times the lead has changed in that race ("Gemini retakes Sports after 9 h · 4th lead change in this race"). [Claude: AGREE]

3. Visual overall lead bar: Include a horizontal stacked bar chart in the header to visually represent each AI's share of the overall total profit at a glance.
4. Auto-generated Weekly Recap: Schedule a Sunday summary post across all socials highlighting the week's biggest win, worst loss, and major standings changes.
